tipsForUsing.title: Tips for using
tipsForUsing.line1: Step 1: Choose the type of test which you wish to create.
tipsForUsing.line2: Step 2: Enter the HTTP method and url of the webpage you wish to test. Then choose one or more locations. A location represents a deployed Synthetic Point of Presence.
tipsForUsing.line3: Step 3: Choose the test frequency (1 ~ 120 minutes).
tipsForUsing.line4: Step 4: In the Name and Description section, enter a meaningful name for your test in the Name field. Add a description of the purpose of your test to the Description field.

whenToUse.line1: Use an HTTP Script test and Node.js based script to test the sequence of multiple Rest APIs

tipsForUsing.line1: Step 1: Choose the type of test which you wish to create.
tipsForUsing.line2: Step 2: Use the Upload the script option to upload a node.js test script file. Then choose one or more locations. A location represents a deployed Synthetic Point of Presence.
tipsForUsing.line3: Step 3: Choose the test frequency (1 ~ 120 minutes).
tipsForUsing.line4: Step 4: In the Name of the test and Description section, enter a meaningful name for your test in the Name field. Add a description of the purpose of your test to the Description field.

popDialog.popUpDialog: Please check the <documentationLink>document</documentationLink> for information about setting Synthetic Monitoring permissions
popDialog.title: Synthetic PoP Commands
popDialog.subTitle: Please use these code templates as a reference. For more information, see <documentationLink>Synthetic PoP Deployment</documentationLink>
popDialog.simpleCode:
helm install synthetic-pop \
	--repo "https://agents.instana.io/helm" \
	--namespace <namespace> \
	--create-namespace \
	--set downloadKey="{{downloadKey}}" \
	--set controller.location="<yourLocationName>;<yourLocationDisplayName>;<yourLocationCountry>;<yourLocationCity>;0;0;<yourLocationDescription>" \
	--set controller.clusterName="<yourClusterName>" \
	--set controller.instanaKey="{{instanaAgentKey}}" \
	--set controller.instanaSyntheticEndpoint="{{syntheticAcceptorURL}}" \
	--set redis.tls.enabled=false \
	--set redis.password="<yourPassword>" \
	synthetic-pop
popDialog.redisCode:
helm install synthetic-pop \
	--repo "https://agents.instana.io/helm" \
	--namespace <namespace> \
	--create-namespace \
	--set downloadKey="{{downloadKey}}" \
	--set controller.location="<yourLocationName>;<yourLocationDisplayName>;<yourLocationCountry>;<yourLocationCity>;0;0;<yourLocationDescription>" \
	--set controller.clusterName="<yourClusterName>" \
	--set controller.instanaKey="{{instanaAgentKey}}" \
	--set controller.instanaSyntheticEndpoint="{{syntheticAcceptorURL}}" \
	--set redis.tls.enabled=true \
	--set redis.tls.secretName="syntheticpop-redis" \
	synthetic-pop
popDialog.tlsInstructions:
If you want to enable Redis TLS, you need to have your X.509 certificate-key pair (`tls.crt`, `tls.key`) and CA root certificate file (`ca.crt`).

If you do not have your key/cert files, you can also use openssl command to generate new ones, see below examples:
popDialog.tlsConfiguration:
openssl genrsa -out tls.key 4096
openssl req -x509 -new -nodes -sha256 -key tls.key -days 3650 -subj '/0=Redis/CN=Certificate Authority' -out ca.crt
openssl req -new -sha256 -key tls.key -subj '/0=Redis/CN=Server' | openssl x509 -req -sha256 -CA ca.crt -CAkey tls.key -CAserial ca.txt -CAcreateserial -days 3650 -out tls.crt
popDialog.tlsSecretInstructions: After key/cert files are provided, use the kubectl command to create a secret.
popDialog.tlsSecretConfigurations:
kubectl create secret generic syntheticpop-redis -n syn \
	--type="kubernetes.io/tls" \
	--from-file=ca.crt="<path/to/ca.crt>" \
	--from-file=tls.crt="<path/to/tls.crt>" \
	--from-file=tls.key="<path/to/tls.key>"
